Optimality theory in evolution centers on traits that provide the greatest net benefit relative to costs compared to alternative traits — not just any benefit exceeding cost, but the best cost-benefit ratio among possible variants.  
Option (A) only states that benefits exceed costs, which is necessary but not sufficient for optimality.  
Option (C) is incorrect because beneficial traits are not "always worth the cost" — if a better alternative exists, the trait may not persist.  
Option (D) focuses only on relative fitness improvement, but not on cost-benefit comparisons among alternative trait forms.  
Option (B) correctly captures the idea of the best return for the cost relative to alternatives, which is the core of optimality theory.  

Final answer: (B)
